name: Pizzica
notes: Pizzica style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). The tarantella of Salento (Puglia, Italy's heel), told with its real history: pizzica belongs to the tarantella family and is bound to TARANTISM — the ritual music-cure documented from the 1600s, in which the tarantata (most often a woman) danced for hours to the tamburello's drive until the 'spider's bite' released her; historians read it as a ritual of release for distress that had no other permitted outlet — a documented phenomenon told with care, not costume. The dance nearly faded with the ritual, then Salento's revival — musicians, scholars, and the Notte della Taranta festival (from 1998, now among Europe's largest music festivals) — brought pizzica roaring back as living joy. Design truths: the springing basic and turns are genuinely solo-trainable; the tamburello's driving 6/8 lives in this app's Rhythm Trainer; the fazzoletto (handkerchief) courtship game and the ronda (the circle where pairs dance at its center) are described honestly and flagged 🤝 — the ronda is entered with people, ideally in Salento's own summer.

seasons.finale: Film yourself clapping and stepping the driving 6/8 through one full pizzica — the frame drum owns you now.
Film the pizzica basic — the light running spring — one full song, landings quiet, joy visible.
Film the traveling turns both directions — skirts or not, the spin is everyone's.
Film the basic with a handkerchief carried and offered to the camera — the courtship game's grammar, rehearsed.
Find pizzica live — a Notte della Taranta screening or stream, an Italian folk festival, a tarantella night — and if a ronda opens, enter it with somebody.

attributes.name: Endurance spring L2
attributes.test: 3 minutes of light continuous spring-stepping — the tarantate danced for HOURS; you need honest minutes

attributes.name: Turn balance L1
attributes.test: 8 traveling turns each direction, soft focus, clean exits — the ronda spins more than it stands

attributes.name: 6/8 drive ear L1
attributes.test: clap the tamburello's compound pulse through one full track without dropping to straight time

nodes.name: The tamburello — the drum that drives the cure
checkpoints: pizzica runs on the tamburello, the frame drum, hammering a driving 6/8 that can run for ten unbroken minutes — it's in this app's Rhythm Trainer
voice, violin, organetto and guitar ride above; the drum never yields
the drive is the point: pizzica's energy is relentless by design — it had a job to do

nodes.name: The revival songbook
checkpoints: Salento's revival bands — Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino (founded 1975, the elder statesmen) and the Notte della Taranta orchestra among them — carried the songbook to world stages
'Pizzica di San Vito' and the classic pizziche are the gateway tracks; build a listening list from the festival's editions
the griko (Salentine Greek) songs in the repertoire remember the region's Greek past — one heel of Italy, many tongues

nodes.name: Tarantism — the ritual cure, told with care
checkpoints: tarantism is documented from the 1600s: the tarantata — most often a woman — danced for hours, sometimes days, to the tamburello until the 'bite of the taranta' released her
historians (Ernesto De Martino's 1959 study 'The Land of Remorse' is the landmark) read it as a ritual of release for distress that had no other permitted outlet in a hard rural world
this history is carried with respect — real people's suffering and survival, not a costume; the joy of today's pizzica stands on their floor

nodes.name: The revival — Notte della Taranta
checkpoints: as the ritual faded in the 20th century the music nearly went with it; Salento's musicians and scholars refused
the Notte della Taranta festival (from 1998, finale in Melpignano) grew into one of Europe's largest music festivals — a hundred thousand people dancing pizzica in a piazza
the revival turned a cure into a celebration without erasing where it came from — the model this whole app tries to honor

nodes.name: Pizzica scherma — the fencing dance
checkpoints: the danza scherma (fencing dance) is pizzica's third face: a mock knife-duel danced with the fingers as blades, famously held all night at Torrepaduli during the Festa di San Rocco (August 15-16)
it carries codes of honor and challenge from an older world — watched respectfully, learned in person from its keepers, never played at
courtship pizzica, the taranta's cure, and the scherma: one drum, three conversations

nodes.name: The pizzica spring
nodes.anchor: the running step that outlasts the drum
checkpoints: a light springing run in place and traveling — small quick steps riding the 6/8, weight forward on the balls of the feet
relaxed and endless beats big and brief: the step must survive the drum's ten minutes
arms lift naturally — open, curved, alive; pizzica arms frame joy
landings quiet; the drum is the percussion, not your heels
mistakes: sprinting the first minute (the tamburello always wins that race)

nodes.name: Traveling turns
checkpoints: the spring carries into spins — traveling turns that orbit an invisible partner, both directions
skirts fly if you wear one; the spin belongs to everyone regardless
soft focus through the turn, clean exit back into the spring — the ronda alternates orbit and approach
mistakes: spotting hard like a pirouette (pizzica turns blur softly; the ronda is not a stage)

nodes.name: The fazzoletto — the handkerchief game
checkpoints: in the courtship pizzica (pizzica de core) the handkerchief is offered, teased, withdrawn — an invitation grammar older than any app
solo rehearsal: carry it, flourish it on the phrase-ends, offer it to the camera and circle away
offering the fazzoletto is asking someone to dance; accepting is answering — consent built into the tradition's own prop

nodes.name: The ronda (with people)
checkpoints: the ronda is the circle: musicians and clappers ring the edge, one pair dances the center, pairs trade in and out
enter when a dancer offers the fazzoletto or the circle's energy invites you; yield the center generously when your turn ends
festivals, tarantella nights, and Salento's own summers keep rondas alive — the circle teaches the rest

nodes.name: Ten minutes with the drum — filmed
checkpoints: one long pizzica (or two chained): spring, turns, fazzoletto flourishes — surviving the drum with joy intact
film the final minute: the test is what's left of you when the tamburello finally stops
somewhere in minute eight you'll understand the tarantate a little — carry that gently

nodes.name: The notte
checkpoints: find pizzica live: Italian folk festivals and tarantella nights run worldwide; the Notte della Taranta streams its finale every August
if the road ever offers you Salento in summer, take it — a piazza of a hundred thousand dancing the old cure as pure celebration
enter a ronda with somebody, offer the fazzoletto, and dance on the floor the tarantate survived to give you
